about.title: S, T, U
about.length_note: Three letters plus a short warm-up fit in about ten minutes. Pause or replay any part as often as you like, so it can run longer.

say.text: Welcome back. Today we meet three letters: S, T and U. For each one we will say its name, its sound, and a word we know.
First, a gentle warm-up. Here are some letters we already know. Look at them, say any you like out loud, and take your time. There is no hurry and no test.

show.text: A B C D E F G H I J K L M N O P Q R

say.text: Let's remember a few of them with a word each. A is for apple. B is for ball. C is for cat. K is for keys. M is for moon.

show.text:
A – apple
B – ball
C – cat
K – keys
M – moon

ask.q: Which word goes with the letter K?
ask.why: K is for keys. Keys start with the 'k' sound.

say.text: Now let's find the next letter. We said P, Q, R. What comes right after R?

ask.q: Which letter comes right after R?
ask.why: The alphabet goes P, Q, R, S. S comes right after R.

say.text: Here is S. The big one is called capital S, or upper case. The small one is lower case. The name of the letter is 'ess'. Say it with me: ess.
The sound of S is a long, soft 'sss', like a snake hissing. Try it: sss. A familiar word is sun. Sss, sun. A grown-up word is street, or sink. Sss, street. Sss, sink.

show.text: A bright yellow sun in a blue sky, with a big letter S beside it. Below it, the words: sun, street, sink.

ask.q: Which word starts with the 'sss' sound?
ask.why: Sun starts with 'sss'. Say it slowly and you can hear the S at the start.

say.text: The two shapes of S look alike. Both are curvy, like a snake. Capital S is tall. Lower case s is small. Look for the curve in both.

show.text:
Upper case: S (tall and curvy)
Lower case: s (small and curvy)

ask.q: Which one is the lower case of S?
ask.why: Lower case s is the small curvy shape, the same shape as S but smaller.

say.text: Next is T. Its name is 'tee'. Say it: tee. The sound of T is a quick little tap, 'tuh'. Your tongue taps behind your top teeth. Try it: t, t, t.
A familiar word is table. T, table. A grown-up word is telephone, or tea. T, telephone. T, tea.

show.text: A wooden table with a cup of tea on it, and a big letter T beside it. Below it, the words: table, telephone, tea.

ask.why: Table starts with the quick 'tuh' sound, which is the sound of T.

say.text: Capital T looks like a table with one leg: a line across the top and a line going down. Lower case t is smaller, with a short line across it, a bit like a little cross.

show.text:
Upper case: T (a line across the top, a line down)
Lower case: t (small, with a short cross line)

ask.q: Which one is the lower case of T?
ask.why: Lower case t is a small line with a short cross line. It is the small partner of T.

say.text: Last today is U. Its name is 'yoo', like the word you. Say it: yoo. The most common sound of U is short and soft: 'uh', as in up. Say it: uh, uh, up.
A familiar word is umbrella. Uh, umbrella. Grown-up words are uncle, and under. Uh, uncle. Uh, under. Sometimes U says its own name, 'yoo', as in unicorn. For now, the 'uh' sound comes first.

show.text: A red umbrella open in the rain, with a big letter U beside it. Below it, the words: umbrella, uncle, under.

ask.q: Which word starts with the short 'uh' sound of U?
ask.why: Umbrella starts with 'uh'. Apple starts with a different sound, and table and sun start with T and S.

say.text: Capital U looks like a cup, open at the top. Lower case u looks the same, only smaller, and with a little tail on the right side. Look for the cup shape.

show.text:
Upper case: U (a cup)
Lower case: u (a small cup, with a little tail)

ask.q: Which one is the lower case of U?
ask.why: Lower case u is a small cup shape. The letter n looks like an upside-down cup, so it is different.

say.text: Let's put all three together. Say each one: name, sound, word. S, sss, sun. T, tuh, table. U, uh, umbrella.

show.text:
S s – sss – sun
T t – tuh – table
U u – uh – umbrella

say.text: One last try. Listen for the first sound of this word: umbrella. Which letter does it start with?

ask.why: Umbrella starts with the short 'uh' sound, and that is the letter U.

say.text: Well done. You met S, T and U today. Take a rest if you like, and come back to say them again whenever you want. Next time we meet V, W and X.

show.text: Well done! Next: V, W, X

notes.topic: S, s: name 'ess', sound 'sss', word sun
T, t: name 'tee', sound 'tuh', word table
U, u: name 'yoo', common sound 'uh', word umbrella
